🔴 **Truncated diffs still produce successful briefs** When a diff ends after a file header, `agent_brief_checked_lines_from_diff` accepts it as complete. The parser records this failure in `truncated_file_sections`, not `limitations`. The brief returns an empty or repository-fallback success for an incomplete patch.
Learn more A textual diff section can have `---` and `+++` headers but no validated hunk body. The bounded parser records this as `ParsedDiff::truncated_file_sections` ([ParsedDiff](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/1a525eaaba07bb416a83a4f4d76c833a20cb5256/crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/parse.rs#L65-L88 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/parse.rs:65-88")), independently of `limitations`. The normal analysis pipeline converts a positive count into a `MalformedDiff` limitation ([truncation gate](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/1a525eaaba07bb416a83a4f4d76c833a20cb5256/crates/ripr/src/analysis/pipeline.rs "crates/ripr/src/analysis/pipeline.rs")). The new brief gate checks only `limitations`, so a cut-off patch reaches ranking as if complete. **Example:** A patch containing `diff --git a/src/lib.rs b/src/lib.rs\n--- a/src/lib.rs\n+++ b/src/lib.rs\n` has one truncated section and no parser limitations. On a repository with an actionable seam, `agent brief --diff` emits exit 0 and a repository-fallback seam instead of refusing the incomplete input. **Recommended fix:** Check `parsed.truncated_file_sections` in `agent_brief_checked_lines_from_diff` before projecting changed lines. Emit `diff_input_unsupported` with the malformed/truncation reason and recovery. Add a CLI control for both a header-only patch and an ordinary hunk followed by a truncated section.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Path-like hunk text wrongly refuses briefs** When an added line starts `++ ` and contains over 516 slashes, `agent_brief_checked_lines_from_diff` rejects a valid patch. The bounded parser checks raw `+++ ` lines for path depth before recognizing hunk content. The brief now exits 2 for this ordinary edit.
Learn more The new brief path calls the bounded parser, while the old path used the unbounded parser. Its [stream admission](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/1a525eaaba07bb416a83a4f4d76c833a20cb5256/crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/parse/stream.rs#L69-L75 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/parse/stream.rs:69-75") runs on every raw line before the parser checks whether it is inside a hunk. The [depth test](https://github.com/effortlessmetrics/ripr-swarm/blob/1a525eaaba07bb416a83a4f4d76c833a20cb5256/crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/path.rs#L14-L18 "crates/ripr/src/analysis/diff/path.rs:14-18") treats every line beginning `+++ ` as a path header, including added hunk payload. This creates a new brief refusal for valid patches with slash-heavy lines. **Example:** A valid textual hunk adds a line starting with `++ ` followed by 517 `/` characters. Its diff payload starts `+++ ` and has 517 slashes. The brief rejects it as `diff_path_too_deep`, whereas the previous brief parser reads it as an added line. **Recommended fix:** Make the bounded parser apply path-depth admission only to actual file headers, after accounting for its hunk and section state. Keep the file-count bound and actual path-header depth refusals intact; add a hunk-payload control to the brief tests.
--- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
